acceptanceCriteria: docs/SPEC-DRIVEN-DEVELOPMENT.md defines the block and its NOT_RUN default.
The spec index check validates the block shape without requiring it on every spec.
At least one spec with a known platform gap (corvint-tasks-user-service-v0.md) carries the block.
body: Idea source: Arize Phoenix (github.com/arize-ai/phoenix), reviewed 2026-10-05. Phoenix is Elastic License 2.0 with a patent notice, so this is a clean-room idea only: no Phoenix code, text or tests may be copied into AGPL Corvint. Idea: Phoenix specs open with a matrix of where each claim was verified (backend versions, interpreter versions), distinguish the language floor from the product support floor, state that behaviour was executed rather than reasoned about, and declare anything outside the matrix unverified. The spec plus its conformance tests is the authority; user docs are a curated derivative. Corvint records platform gaps in build logs and NOT_RUN lists (e.g. V1-0804 Linux-only helpers, platform qualification under V1-0697), but not in a uniform spec header where agents read first (the Agent digest). Proposal: an optional, machine-checkable Verified-on block in the spec digest (OS, arch, Go toolchain, host type, date, evidence pointer), validated by the spec index, with absent rows meaning NOT_RUN.
title: Spec header: "verified on" matrix separating requirement floor, product floor and unverified platforms
